summary: Correct the consonant in huḍoy-awo
rationale: The supplied 24/305 reads “u huḏoyawo”, with ḏ, not emphatic ḍ. Other glossary quotations from the same story consistently use huḏoyo (e.g. kly III, 24/300). This is a consonant error, not the permitted d/ḏ normalization.

summary: Restore the word rawmo (pond)
rationale: The supplied JL 9.9/11 reads “kətlan rawmo rabṯo”. The same passage under ylf I also has rawmo. The w and m were transposed in this entry.

summary: Restore the missing la- in lašana
rationale: The supplied 64/30 reads “mawḏaʕle əšme lašana”. The entry drops the initial la- of lašana. Restoring it preserves the corpus wording and the recipient expressed by the translation.

summary: New idiom: aḏəʕ/oḏəʕ b-qadro 'jemandes Wert erkennen'

rationale: A conditional prohibition frames this as a threat of consequences, distinct from R1's free-choice responsibility formula. Single attestation; search šuġlox found no glossary match; broader šuġl search was not exhaustive (74 hits, 25 displayed). English is supplied machine translation.

summary: The aggregate routine counts support frequent I.1 Infectum (1006), I.2 Preterit Intransitive (184), I.1 Preterit Intransitive (127), I.2 Infectum (107), and I.1 Infectum-wa (91). Counts are reader assignments, not newly checked tokens.

Zero-marked nominal stimuli are attested with clear qaṭəl: Aḏiʕono kul mede at Hors 2/119; aḏiʕo i qimayḏan at Lahdo Traitor 1/54; aḏəʕ u aḥuno and aḏəʕ i aṯto du aḥuno at 78/218. A categorical ban on such stimuli is untenable. The fronted palace resumed by -le (Hors 2/50), reciprocals and consciousness expressions should be distinguished from these ordinary nominal stimuli.

The same speaker alternates zero i qimayḏan, bu i qimayḏan, bu qadrayḏan and zero i qimayḏan in Lahdo Traitor 1/54. Preserve bu i exactly; a general case rule cannot be inferred from this one repaired utterance.

Knowledge states occur with Preterit Intransitive; acquisitions, skill knowledge and future knowledge use the Infectum as well. Reduced -wa forms cannot be assigned by German tense or lack of k- alone. Identical əḏʕinawo forms receive a consistent provisional Infectum-wa analysis.

Parenthetic aḏiʕat/kuḏʕat comprehension checks retain implicit discourse stimuli (40/30; MAC NE Keze/24). The choice/responsibility idiom differs pragmatically, without another lexical sense. The shot idiom has a personified inanimate subject.

Detransitive Infectum ranges from known-state and generic recognizability to a future identification event; b- and m- can introduce diagnostic evidence, while m ḥḏoḏe marks the things compared. Detransitive Infectum-wa at MAC Ishaq old houses/86 supplies a secure missing box.

III reports content, informs recipients, and introduces people. Omitted audiences in 94/152,157,221 remain III.1; adverse reporting with an ʕal-target at PrS 40/8 merits a lettered construction. The 74/11 reciprocal introduction adds no new sense.

The Hors 2/126 acquaintance passage duplicates inherited MM 126; do not add it again. JL 14.8/19 contains both I.1 Infectum-wa and I.2 Preterit Intransitive; an example’s box does not classify every verb in it.

Jan Beṯ-Şawoce round 2. All supplied English is project machine translation, not an edition translation; analyses and sense decisions rest on the Turoyo. Quoted English is copied verbatim and labelled as machine translation. Round-1 proposals are the baseline and are not repeated in this JSON.

The material includes interviews, quoted speech and written discussion; it is not uniformly literary prose. The routine counts are inherited reader summaries (including I.1 Infectum 930 and Infectum-wa 141); only the 131 supplied tokens were individually checked.

Reduced əḏʕiwo, əḏʕanwo and əḏʕatwole are provisionally treated as Infectum-wa consistently with R1; Jan 1.15/558,591, 1.22/1151, 1.47/2106 and 1.59/2950 do not securely establish a new Preterit-wa cell. Jan 1.16/644 begins with ability to take a photograph, rather than a free-standing knowledge state.

Repeated kuḏaʕ/kuḏəʕ lacks an expected first-person ending in first-person discourse, including explicit əno at Jan 2.18/3747. Preserve the source; no emendation or new person paradigm follows. Fused kəḏʕalla/kəḏʕalle and kuḏaʕnox require separate segmentation checks.

Personal acquaintance at Jan 2.4/501,876,915,934 and 2.31/4948 belongs to I.1; the readers' I.2 assignments do not show acquisition or identification. Aḏəʕoli at Jan 1.23/1210 instead presents recognition after identifying speech and belongs to I.2. -li at Jan 2.4/915 is not securely a third-person stimulus suffix: the nearby mention of Nəʕmo does not license changing its person value.

yadoʕaṯṯe, yaḏoʕo and Yaḏoʕe (Jan 2.1/2; 2.8/1904; 2.28/4593; 2.35/5589) are learned lexical knower/expert formations. They do not securely establish a productive native Part act. box. Literary Syriac yaḏʕin and məṯyaḏʕina at Jan 2.10/2733,2735 are excluded as Turoyo paradigm evidence.

III Infectum-wa at Jan 1.39/1741 fills a form gap; b ḥaq diḏan marks content and audience is recoverable. Jan 1.49/2214 occurs beside giving lessons; instruction is contextual, within III.1. III Detransitive covers legal notification (Jan 1.47/2106), inferential recognition from fruit (3.56/1645), disclosure with a retained -la recipient/location (3.56/1687), and abstract closeness becoming known (4.I/137).

The negative and affirmative knowing formulas do not independently establish tell, think, self-awareness or decide lexical senses. b ruḥi plus a content clause (Jan 2.1/8) is ordinary self-awareness within I.1; kuḏaʕnolox (2.2/169) has an addressee and an understood knowledge stimulus.
Confirm sexual consummation as a conventional reciprocal euphemism in JTM 1.3/38; one attestation supports the restricted machine-proposed I.1a, not a claim of wide distribution.

Confirm the Midyat reduced past paradigm: əḏʕiwayna, əḏʕinawo, əḏʕiwo, əḏʕə́newa, ləḏʕiwa, Əḏʕowa and ləḏʕayno. The audit provisionally uses Infectum-wa; no new Preterit-wa cell is published from ambiguous forms.
Check kaḏiʕat at 58/277 for ko-Preterit versus dialectal Infectum; decide whether the learned noun yaḏoʕo at 60/315 belongs in the verbal boxes.

Verify anomalous source forms without silent emendation: Lahdo kәzʕina and interrupted kəḏ...; PrS final ḥ/ṭ spelling (koḏaḥ, koḏəḥ, Kuḏʕəṭ), unsuffixed first-person koḏaʕ, kuḏaʕli; Ritter koḏaʕ”e and koḏaʕʕƏ. Confirm suffix/person analyses of MAC contracted forms, 29/134 əḏʕilan, 81/78 iḏiʕin and 82/58 Aḏiʕi.
Does b-qadro only express appreciating worth, or also a fitting reward? Does d əḏʕət ruḥux at 53/169 represent a separate warning formula?
The consciousness idiom is cited LB 163 in the inherited entry but occurs at supplied Talay 1/164. Verify edition/verse mapping before changing the inherited citation.
Confirm adverse-report III.1a and distinguish ʕal-target from ʕal-topic. Does the wedding reciprocal overlap ordinary acquaintance in other dialects?
Confirm the reduced past paradigm əḏʕiwo / əḏʕanwo / əḏʕatwole against Infectum-wa before assigning any Jan example to Preterit-wa.
Are yadoʕaṯṯe / yaḏoʕo / yaḏoʕe synchronically borrowed nouns/adjectives or verbal Part act.? No new box is proposed.
Confirm mdaʕanwo / mdaʕewo (Jan 2.3/291–292): reduced Detransitive Infectum-wa or a known-state nominal predicate? Their stem attribution remains provisional.
Confirm kuḏaʕnox at Jan 1.26/1276, Laḏəʕnən at 1.45/1965, kəḏʕatli at 2.4/915, and the missing person endings; do not substitute the machine translation's person.
Does kmiḏoʕi at Jan 2.10/2736 introduce known status to foreign observers, and is nawʕ man nəxroye a source/observer phrase? No agent syntax is asserted.
Confirm whether III.1b characterization and the conditional kəḏʕət šuġlox threat are conventional beyond their single attestations.
Verify the verse range for the composite tent quotation

rationale: The final clause is present in 78/63, so the automatic suggestion must not replace it. However, the preceding silver-ball clause is explicitly supplied as 78/62. The opening sentence about the sheikh’s tent is in neither supplied verse. summary: Make the second verb agree with singular man
rationale: The coordinated German clauses have the subject “man”: “ergriff man ... und überantwortete ...”. The plural ending in überantworteten is an agreement slip; it is also present in the supplied edition translation.

summary: An institution can be experiencer; knowing worth alternates with recognising/appreciating it. This participant extension creates no independent sense.
Detransitive known-state predicates include food kinds and established days; these are participant extensions.
Value recognition extends to land and life; b- marks the valued domain.
A character may present a false belief as knowledge; do not infer a separate think sense from German hielt.

The mutually alike manufactured roses support R1's Detransitive distinction subsense; m ḥḏoḏe is not repeated as a complement here, so this supports the meaning rather than demonstrating that government.

Aḏəʕno aḥ ḥadisat diḏe and adəʕno u šəkəl di ʕiyeše provide explicit unmarked nominal stimuli with qaṭəl, strengthening R1's counterexamples. Discourse parentheticals, object resumption and uncertain -wa forms are separate evidence.
Known status extends to liturgical content that has already been settled; no separate predetermined lexical sense is established.
